title: Software Testing Pyramid
description: Keep this beside the test plan: unit tests form the broad base, while end-to-end checks stay selective.
note: The pyramid places many unit tests below fewer integration and end-to-end tests. I should check whether our Life Lab test plan has the same balance.
taskTitle: Compare the Life Lab test plan with the testing pyramid

title: Software Architecture Activities
description: A compact reference for explaining the activities involved in architecture design during the project presentation.
note: This diagram groups software-architecture work into a small set of activities. Use it to structure the architecture section of the presentation rather than listing technologies without a design story.
taskTitle: Outline the architecture slide around the diagram's activities

title: Git Branching Workflow
description: Reference for explaining feature branches and the route back to the main development line.
note: The image shows a branching workflow rather than a flat sequence of commits. I can use it to explain where a feature branch is reviewed before it rejoins the main line.
taskTitle: Draw the project's actual branch flow beside this reference

title: Bloom's Taxonomy Study Ladder
description: Use the levels as a prompt to turn passive revision into explanation and application exercises.
note: The chart rises from knowledge and comprehension to application, analysis, synthesis and evaluation. For exam review, I should include a practice question above simple recall.
taskTitle: Write one application question for this week's revision

title: Research Cycle
description: A reminder that a research question, evidence and interpretation need another pass after an initial result.
note: The cycle presents research as iterative. I need to record what evidence changes the question, not treat the first explanation as the final answer.
taskTitle: Revisit the project research question after reviewing evidence

title: Eisenhower Priority Matrix
description: Useful for separating urgent deadlines from important work that needs protected time.
note: The matrix separates urgency from importance. Before filling tomorrow's plan, I should identify important project work that is not yet urgent.
taskTitle: Sort tomorrow's work by urgency and importance

title: Gantt Schedule Example
description: A visual reference for communicating project activity timing and dependencies in the demo presentation.
note: The chart places tasks against time, making overlap and sequencing visible. I can use this format to explain our project milestones without claiming the example dates are ours.

title: IPA Pronunciation Chart
description: Reference for checking unfamiliar sounds during English speaking and listening practice.
note: The IPA chart groups speech sounds by how they are produced. I should use one symbol at a time with an actual pronunciation example, not try to memorize the whole chart at once.
taskTitle: Practice two unfamiliar IPA sounds with example words

title: Kanban Board Example
description: A simple board to discuss how project work moves between visible stages.
note: The board makes work states visible in columns. For our project, a useful board should reveal work in progress instead of hiding every task in one long list.

title: Structured Programming Flowchart
description: Keep as a visual example of explicit branches and control flow for algorithm review.
note: The flowchart uses decision paths to show how execution proceeds. I should trace each branch with a small input before translating it into code.
taskTitle: Trace both paths in the flowchart with sample inputs

title: PostgreSQL Internal Architecture
description: Processes, memory and files in one reference for the database architecture review.
note: The diagram separates client/server processes, memory and files. It is a useful map before reading about how PostgreSQL handles a request, but the arrows need careful explanation.
taskTitle: Explain one PostgreSQL request path using the diagram

provider: Wikimedia Commons / University of Warwick photo
title: University Computer Lab
description: A real campus computer-lab reference for a presentation about collaborative study spaces.
note: The photograph shows rows of desktop computers in a university lab. It can illustrate a learning environment, but it does not by itself prove anything about how students use the space.
taskTitle: Write an accurate caption for the computer-lab slide

title: Linear Regression Illustration
description: Scatter points and a fitted line for reviewing the difference between observed data and a model.
note: The points represent observations and the line represents a fitted trend. I should explain that the line summarizes a relationship rather than passing through every point.
taskTitle: Explain the plotted observations and fitted line in plain language

title: GTK Software Architecture
description: A concrete stack diagram for comparing responsibilities across software layers.
note: The diagram places GTK above supporting libraries such as GDK and GLib. It is an example of layered dependencies, not a model of our React application.
taskTitle: Compare the idea of layers with the project architecture

title: HTTP Request and Response Example
description: A labeled request/response exchange to support an API walkthrough; the image labels are in German.
note: The image labels the blocks of an HTTP request and response. I should use it for message structure only; the example's historical protocol details require checking against current HTTP documentation.
taskTitle: Annotate the HTTP message parts for an API walkthrough

title: Two-Series Bar Chart
description: A simple chart reference for discussing how color distinguishes two data series.
note: The bars use two contrasting colors to distinguish series. The chart is a visual-format example; it should not be presented as evidence about the project's own measurements.
taskTitle: Choose a clear legend for the project results chart
